candidates.attacker_control: The fileName argument of the public normalize(String), normalize(String, boolean), normalizeNoEndSeparator(String) and normalizeNoEndSeparator(String, boolean) APIs, i.e. untrusted file names, URL paths, or archive entry names supplied to an application that uses these methods as its traversal-sanitization step.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked doNormalize for any post-normalization rejection of '.'-containing prefixes (none between :350-444); searched the whole tree for isValidHostName/hostnamePart validation helpers (zero matches, so no UNC hostname validation exists in this snapshot); verified getPrefixLength's only host-related rejection is the empty-host cases posUnix==2/posWin==2 (:674), which '..' does not trigger; confirmed the double-dot loop's guard i==prefix+2 (:411-413) only rejects a second dot-dot at the start of the post-prefix region, not the one embedded in the prefix; confirmed the snapshot has no tests bundled (source tree is main/site only), so behavior was verified by manual tracing rather than execution.
candidates.impact: Callers that use normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() as a path-traversal defense can be tricked into accepting an output still containing a leading '..' segment. When the result is joined to a base directory and opened/deleted/streamed, the OS resolves the segment and escapes one directory above the intended base, giving unauthorized read/write/delete in the parent directory. On Windows the returned value is a UNC-shaped path whose "server" is '..', which is similarly mis-resolved by downstream file APIs. Because the flaw is in a widely used utility method, the blast radius is broad across applications that rely on it for sanitization.
candidates.prerequisites: An application passes attacker-influenced input to FilenameUtils.normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() and then trusts or resolves the returned value against a base directory (e.g. new File(base, normalized) or equivalent path join). No in-library sink exists; impact therefore depends on downstream caller usage. The retained leading '..' escapes the base by one directory level (the input cannot carry further '..' through the prefix, since a second dot-dot sequence after the prefix is correctly rejected at :411-413), so the traversal is limited, matching a sanitization-bypass rather than arbitrary full traversal.
candidates.root_cause: getPrefixLength() treats any separator-delimited text as a valid UNC hostname, rejecting only an empty host (FilenameUtils.java:671-679). It therefore accepts "." and ".." as the "server" part (prefix = length including the following separator, e.g. 5 for "//../foo"). doNormalize() then starts its double-dot scan at i = prefix + 2 (:408), so the "../" that lies inside the prefix region (indices 2-4) is never examined or removed; no post-hoc validation of the result exists, and the method returns the unmodified string via new String(array, 0, size - 1) (:443). The contract documented in the same file (:179, :185) says such inputs should return null.
candidates.title: FilenameUtils.normalize() leaves '..' in UNC-like paths, bypassing path-traversal sanitization
candidates.trace: Manual source trace (no execution): (1) input "//../foo": getPrefixLength sees ch0/ch1 both separators, finds the next separator at index 4 and returns 5 without validating the hostname substring(2,4)==".." (:671-679); (2) doNormalize fixes separators, appends a trailing separator, and enters the double-dot loop at i = prefix+2 = 7 (:408), so indices 2-4 are outside the scan and the "../" is never collapsed; (3) no other check rejects the remaining ".." and the method returns new String(array, 0, size-1) == "//../foo" (:443). The same trace with "\\..\foo" yields "\\..\foo" (Windows separator form; prefix computed identically because isSeparator matches both characters). The documented examples at :179 and :185 expect null for these shapes. The same defect is reachable through all four public normalize/normalizeNoEndSeparator overloads (:196-198, :243-246, :290-292, :337-340).
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution was performed; the exact resolution behavior depends on the downstream caller and on OS path semantics (leading '//' treatment, UNC parsing). The precise historical fix shape and whether any released 2.7 build differs from this snapshot were not checked (no external sources consulted). Impact assumes a caller that relies on normalization for containment; absent such a caller, this is a contract violation of the documented null-return behavior rather than a directly exploitable bug.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper neutralization of '..' in path normalization / path traversal sanitization bypass

coverage_summary: Source scope: 168 files / 168 source_root_files, no binary exclusions; the P1 index reports complete coverage (168/168 indexed, no missing files, no hash mismatches) and is explicitly syntactic navigation only. This snapshot contains only src/main, src/site, assembly and build metadata (no src/test). I inspected the full FilenameUtils implementation paths relevant to the candidate (getPrefixLength :630-683, doNormalize :350-444, public normalize APIs), pom.xml version context, and changes.xml 2.7 section, and ran targeted searches (traversal, IO-655, CVE, isValidHostName, hostnamePart) across the tree. Other packages (input/output streams, file filters, comparators, monitor, serialization, FileUtils/IOUtils) were only spot-checked via search/navigation, not exhaustively read line by line, so unreviewed areas remain.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or scanners were run; the candidate behavior is a manual source trace and is not runtime-confirmed.
The snapshot has no test sources, so documented-vs-actual behavior could not be cross-checked against bundled tests.
The P1 index provides syntactic candidates only (calls/containment/inheritance), not data flow or reachability; edges were verified against source text where used.

No external references (patches, advisories, CVE databases) were consulted, and this run is independent of any other case or configuration.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Commons IO snapshot (168 main/site files, version 2.7-SNAPSHOT per pom.xml:27, changes.xml latest release section only through IO-577). The strongest source-supported issue is in FilenameUtils: the UNC/prefix handling in getPrefixLength() accepts "."/".." as a "host" and doNormalize() never scans inside the prefix region, so normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() return inputs such as "//../foo" or "\\\\..\\foo" with the ".." segment intact, contradicting the documented contract ("/.." and "//server/../bar" -> null) and defeating callers that rely on normalization to remove traversal segments. One candidate submitted; other leads (XmlStreamReader resource consumption, FileSystemUtils Windows command construction) were not strong enough to meet the one-candidate bar and are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
